items.title: Derek Brown interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 5, 2021
items.q: my dad had Brubeck’s “Time Out,” a couple other things.

ctx.x: So a couple of things were happening then, one of which, I’m not sure how relevant it is but the change to compact disks from LPs. I wonder if LPs had any role in your life? Because I was one of those guys who used to read the liner notes like to get my jazz history.

Well okay, the bad news is it wasn’t LPs but the good news because this is still before Spotify and Napster, the CDs, they were smaller of course but they often still had booklets. And I love that stuff. I was just talking with a friend a little bit ago about how every CD we owned it was that top to bottom, every word you read, I mean one it was just something to do while you’re listening to it. Also, you know, being kind of, I was kind of newer to jazz. Like my parents didn’t raise me so much on jazz so to…
Was there a first saxophone player that you heard and you wondered, all right, who is that, and then you started looking for that name?
